text: If you were the devil, and maybe you are, what would you do?
That is quite a hello. I am not the devil. But in a pretend story? I would start with a little trick.
Fire? Horns? A giant red fork?
No. I would keep people so busy looking at little screens that they forget to look at each other.
So my phone is the devil?
No. A phone is a tool. It can help you call your grandma. Or help you ignore your grandma while she is sitting next to you.
All right. What is your next little trick?
Make people think everyone else has a better life. A bigger house. A nicer cake. Even a happier dog.
My dog eats socks. Should I be worried about his life choices?
He seems quite happy with his socks. But people can miss their own good things while counting someone else's.
What would you do after that?
Make every small fight feel huge. Get people shouting so loudly that nobody hears what the other person is trying to say.
So the devil runs the family group chat?
In this story, he would be very busy there. Then comes the sneaky bit. Tell people that one small kind thing will not help.
But if lots of little mean things can make a big mess, could little kind things help clean it up?
Yes. Hold a door. Say sorry. Put the phone down. Ask your friend how they feel. Small does not mean useless.
So we fight the devil with sorry and a cup of tea?
In our story, yes. His big scary plan gets spoiled by little acts of kindness. Hard to look scary when someone offers you a biscuit.
I am going to call my grandma. Then check what my dog is chewing.
A lovely plan. Save the grandma. Save the socks. What is one small good thing you could do for someone right now?
